story.iWant: specialized analysis agent that can perform calculations and reasoning over retrieved data
story.soThat: analytical questions can be answered autonomously
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Implement analysis_agent function with @tool decorator (AC1, AC2) - 4 hours - 1.1: Create raglite/agentic/agents/analysis_agent.py file - 1.2: Implement @tool async def analysis_agent(data, analysis_type, context) with AWS Strands decorator - 1.3: Define AnalysisResult Pydantic model in raglite/agentic/state.py - 1.4: Implement 4 analysis type handlers: yoy_growth, variance, trend, percentage - 1.5: Add error handling for invalid data or analysis types
- Task 2: Integrate Claude Haiku for numerical reasoning (AC3) - 3 hours - 2.1: Import Claude client from raglite/shared/clients.py - 2.2: Create structured prompt templates for each analysis type - 2.3: Implement LLM reasoning call with Claude Haiku model - 2.4: Parse LLM response and extract reasoning explanation - 2.5: Add retry logic for Claude API errors (429/500 status codes) - 2.6: Validate numerical accuracy of LLM-generated formulas
- Task 3: Create unit tests for analysis agent (AC4) - 3 hours - 3.1: Create tests/unit/agentic/test_analysis_agent.py - 3.2: Mock Claude API to return synthetic reasoning - 3.3: Test YoY growth calculation: {"Q3_2023": 10.0, "Q3_2024": 12.0} → +20% - 3.4: Test variance analysis: {"budget": 100.0, "actual": 85.0} → -15% under budget - 3.5: Test trend detection: {"Q1": 10, "Q2": 12, "Q3": 14} → increasing trend - 3.6: Test percentage calculation: {"part": 25.0, "whole": 100.0} → 25% - 3.7: Test error handling (invalid data, missing keys, LLM API failure) - 3.8: Validate test execution time <100ms (no real LLM calls)
- Task 4: Create integration test for 3-agent workflow (AC5) - 4 hours - 4.1: Create tests/integration/test_retrieval_analysis_synthesis_workflow.py - 4.2: Implement 3-agent workflow test: Retrieval → Analysis → Synthesis - 4.3: Use real Qdrant instance (requires docker-compose up -d) - 4.4: Use real Claude Haiku for analysis reasoning (budget LLM calls) - 4.5: Use MockSynthesisAgent from Story 3.1 - 4.6: Test agent coordination via AWS Strands orchestrator - 4.7: Validate workflow execution time <8s - 4.8: Validate analysis results passed correctly to synthesis agent
- Task 5: Update orchestrator configuration (AC1) - 1 hour - 5.1: Add analysis_agent to orchestrator tools list in raglite/agentic/orchestrator.py - 5.2: Update orchestrator system prompt to include analysis_agent usage - 5.3: Test orchestrator can discover and call analysis_agent - 5.4: Validate orchestrator logs show analysis_agent execution
- Task 6: Document agent usage and integration (AC1) - 1 hour - 6.1: Update docs/architecture/3-1-agentic-workflow-guide.md with analysis_agent example - 6.2: Document analysis_agent signature and AnalysisResult format - 6.3: Add code example showing orchestrator calling analysis_agent - 6.4: Document 4 supported analysis types with usage examples

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
AC1: Analysis agent defined with @tool decorator per AWS Strands framework - Agent decorated with @tool decorator from AWS Strands - Agent signature follows Strands tool conventions - Agent registered with orchestrator as callable tool - Agent supports 4 analysis types: YoY growth, variance, trend detection, percentages
AC2: Agent accepts financial data and analysis instruction, returns AnalysisResult - Input: Financial data points (Dict[str, float]), analysis_type (str), optional context (str) - Output: JSON-serialized AnalysisResult with calculation, value, formatted_value, reasoning, data_points_used - Supports analysis types: "yoy_growth", "variance", "trend", "percentage" - Returns structured calculation formulas (e.g., "(12M - 10M) / 10M = 0.20")
AC3: Agent uses Claude Haiku for numerical reasoning with structured prompts - Calls Claude Haiku via shared client from raglite/shared/clients.py - Structured prompts ensure numerical accuracy (formula validation) - Reasoning explains calculation logic and business interpretation - Error handling for LLM API failures (return error metadata)
AC4: Agent tested with sample analytical tasks (unit tests) - Unit test validates YoY growth calculation accuracy - Unit test validates variance analysis (budget vs actual) - Unit test validates trend detection (increasing/decreasing/stable) - Unit test validates percentage calculations - Mocked Claude API prevents external dependencies - Test execution time <100ms (framework overhead only)
AC5: Agent integrates with Retrieval Agent for data access (integration test) - Integration test executes Retrieval → Analysis → Synthesis 3-agent workflow - Test uses real Qdrant instance (requires docker-compose up) - Test validates agent coordination via AWS Strands orchestrator - Test validates analysis results passed correctly to synthesis agent - Test execution time <8s (includes real search + LLM latency)

story-context.constraints: - Use AWS Strands @tool decorator pattern (established in Story 3.1-3.2) - Return JSON-serialized output (Strands framework requirement) - Claude Haiku model for analysis reasoning (5x faster than Sonnet, 10x cheaper) - Analysis agent budget: <800ms p50, <1.2s p95 execution time (NFR5 performance constraint) - Individual agent timeout: 15s max (NFR26 - enforced by error_handler.py) - Import Claude client from raglite/shared/clients.py (no new client creation) - Add agent to orchestrator tools list via register_tools() method - Follow error handling patterns from error_handler.py (timeout, retry, graceful degradation) - Use structured logging with logger.info(extra={...}) for agent execution tracking - Mock Claude API in unit tests (no real LLM calls, prevent API costs) - Use real Claude Haiku in integration tests (budget ~$0.10 per test run) - Use MockSynthesisAgent for integration tests (Story 3.4 not ready yet) - Test execution time: Unit tests <100ms, Integration tests <8s - 4 supported analysis types: yoy_growth, variance, trend, percentage - Formula validation: Ensure calculated values match formula strings - Error metadata: Return structured error info on failures (no hard crashes)

interface.name: analysis_agent
AnalysisResult
interface.signature: class AnalysisResult(BaseModel): calculation: str # Formula string (e.g., "(12M - 10M) / 10M = 0.20") value: float # Numerical result (e.g., 0.20) formatted_value: str # Human-readable format (e.g., "+20%") reasoning: str # LLM-generated explanation data_points_used: Dict[str, float] # Original data dictionary

interface.name: get_claude_client
interface.signature:
def get_claude_client() -> anthropic.Anthropic: """Returns shared Claude API client instance.
Use model="claude-3-5-haiku-20241022" for analysis agent. """

interface.name: Orchestrator.register_tools
interface.signature:
def register_tools(self, tools: List[Callable]) -> None: """Register custom tools with orchestrator.
Usage: from raglite.agentic.agents.analysis_agent import analysis_agent orchestrator.register_tools([analysis_agent]) """

tests.standards: All tests use pytest framework with async support (pytest-asyncio). Unit tests mock external dependencies (Claude API, Qdrant) to ensure fast execution (<100ms) and prevent API costs. Integration tests use real Qdrant instance and real Claude Haiku API (budget ~$0.10 per run). Tests follow existing patterns from Story 3.2 retrieval_agent tests. Code coverage target: 80%+ for raglite/agentic/ module. Test naming convention: test_{component}_{scenario} (e.g., test_analysis_agent_yoy_growth_calculation).
tests.locations: - tests/unit/agentic/ (unit tests for agents) - tests/integration/ (integration tests for workflows) - tests/conftest.py (shared fixtures)
